# JDK Flight Recorder (JFR) Metadata

The JFR `print` option, discussed in the [JFR Print](../jfr-print/README.md)
example, provides event data without its metadata. Metadata describes the event
type, including its name, category, labels, descriptions, and field layout. It
is the same for all events of the same type, so there is little value in
repeating it with every event.

This example shows how to inspect that metadata with the `jfr metadata` command.
The recording is used only as input for the tool; the focus is the event schema
rather than the event values.

More information about the JFR `metadata` option is available as part of the
command’s help.

```shell
jfr --help metadata
```

The JFR `metadata` option takes the following options.

```
Display event metadata, such as labels, descriptions and field layout

 jfr metadata [--categories <filter>]
              [--events <filter>]
              [<file>]

  --categories <filter>   Select events matching a category name.
                          The filter is a comma-separated list of names,
                          simple and/or qualified, and/or quoted glob patterns

  --events <filter>       Select events matching an event name.
                          The filter is a comma-separated list of names,
                          simple and/or qualified, and/or quoted glob patterns

  <file>                  Location of the recording file (.jfr)

If the <file> parameter is omitted, metadata from the JDK where
the 'jfr' tool is located will be used


Example usage:

 jfr metadata

 jfr metadata --events jdk.ThreadStart recording.jfr

 jfr metadata --events CPULoad,GarbageCollection

 jfr metadata --categories 'GC,JVM,Java*'

 jfr metadata --events 'Thread*'
```

This example uses the `--events` option to print the metadata for one event type
from a recording.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- [JDK Mission Control (JMC)](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/products-jmc9-downloads.html)

## Build the application

Build the application before creating the recording.

```shell
./mvnw clean package
```

(*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created

```shell
tree --sort=name './target/libs'
```

There should be one JAR file

```
./target/libs
└── jfr-metadata-1.0.0.jar

1 directory, 1 file
```

The following commands write JFR files into the `jfr` directory. Reset the
directory so the recording created by this run is easy to find.

```shell
rm -rf './jfr'
mkdir -p './jfr'
```

## Inspect event metadata

1. Run the application and capture a recording

   ```shell
   java \
     -XX:StartFlightRecording=duration=30s,delay=5s,name='Metadata',filename='./jfr/demo.jfr' \
     -jar './target/libs/jfr-metadata-1.0.0.jar'
   ```

   The application will terminate automatically after 40 seconds.

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JFR file was created.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './jfr'
   ```

   The recording

   ```
   ./jfr
   └── demo.jfr

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

2. Print the event metadata

   ```shell
   jfr metadata --events 'jdk.CPUInformation' './jfr/demo.jfr'
   ```

   This prints the metadata for the `jdk.CPUInformation` event type.

   ```java
   @Name("jdk.CPUInformation")
   @Category({"Operating System", "Processor"})
   @Label("CPU Information")
   @Description("Characteristics and descriptions of the processor(s) the JVM is running on")
   class CPUInformation extends jdk.jfr.Event {
     @Label("Start Time")
     @Timestamp("TICKS")
     long startTime;

     @Label("Type")
     String cpu;

     @Label("Description")
     String description;

     @Unsigned
     @Label("Sockets")
     int sockets;

     @Unsigned
     @Label("Cores")
     int cores;

     @Unsigned
     @Label("Hardware Threads")
     int hwThreads;
   }
   ```

   The output is a Java-like view of the event type. `@Name` is the event name
   used by JFR tools, `@Category` controls where the event appears in JMC,
   `@Label` and `@Description` provide human-readable text, and the class body
   shows the fields captured for this event.

3. (*Optional*) Open the flight recording file with JMC (`./jfr/demo.jfr`).

   ```shell
   jmc -open "$(pwd)/jfr/demo.jfr"
   ```

   JMC is not required for the `jfr metadata` command, but it is useful when you
   want to compare the command-line metadata with the way the event is presented
   in the JMC user interface. Download JMC from
   [Oracle](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/products-jmc9-downloads.html)
   and make sure `jmc` is available on your `PATH`.

   If you have multiple versions of Java installed, you may need to specify
   which one JMC should use. This can be done through the `jmc.ini` file, found
   under the `Eclipse` directory where JMC is installed.

   Add the `-vm` option followed by the path to the `bin` directory, as shown
   next.

   ```
   ...
   -vm
   /Users/aattard/.sdkman/candidates/java/current/bin
   ...
   ```

   This file usually contains other settings too; they are excluded here for
   brevity.
